entries.test: Labour-market studies and reports up to October 2022 on jobs actually displaced by AI, together with the state of AI language understanding at the time.
entries.note: Compound claim. The jobs part is the more testable half.

entries.test: Whether any commercial driverless trucking ran outside test pilots, or any radiologist position was replaced by AI, as of October 2022.
entries.note: He wrote 'every truck I know', a personal scope; the proposition makes it a general claim.
'May yet materialize' has no deadline, and possibility is a matter of principle.

entries.test: Whether any AI system in 2022 showed broad, child-like learning of new skills from very little data, judged against the few-shot learning literature.
entries.note: Few-shot in-context learning in 2022 LLMs is the obvious counterevidence a grader would weigh.

entries.test: Whether any AI system in October 2022 matched human general intelligence across broad tasks, by contemporary benchmarks and expert assessments.
entries.note: The claim is dated to the time of writing.

entries.test: Whether convnet-based systems in 2022 solved most major AI problems such as language understanding, reasoning and planning.
entries.note: The side claim that LeCun contradicted his ZDNet interview is not part of the proposition.

entries.test: Whether AI augmentation tools are widely deployed in occupations, such as radiology and accounting, where full AI replacement has not been achieved.
entries.note: A general conceptual claim. Graded on the deployment record.

entries.test: Whether any 2022 AI system could reliably interpret tax codes well enough to do an accountant's judgement work, such as deciding deductibility.
Radiology job-task analyses, plus the 2022 literature on how convnets perform on image tasks versus unstructured clinical text and history reasoning.
entries.note: Taken from his own embedded tweet.

entries.test: Professional descriptions of radiologists' duties, showing how much of the job is image interpretation versus other tasks.
entries.note: Taken from his own embedded tweet.

entries.test: Whether AI has fully displaced radiologists, meaning the profession is replaced rather than augmented, before January 1, 2033.
entries.note: A public bet in his own tweet. The deadline is after the evaluation date.
A point about what follows logically, not an empirical claim. No evidence would settle it.

entries.test: Whether published evidence in 2022 showed scan-reading AI approaching end-to-end replacement of radiologists.
entries.note: 'No evidence whatsoever' is overstated, but the claim has a shared plain reading.

entries.test: The correlation reported in Caucheteux, Gramfort & King (2022) and whether the result is purely correlational.
entries.note: 'Hardly decisive' is evaluative. The R value and its correlational nature can be checked.

entries.test: The paper's text on variance explained, and any later published correction.
entries.note: The R-squared arithmetic is standard. The question is whether the paper said half.

entries.test: Whether the Caucheteux et al. study shows mechanistic links between GPT-2 and brain processing, or only correlations.
entries.note: An interpretive judgement about the evidence, but its plain reading can be checked.

entries.test: Whether any AI system in 2022 was deployed or shown to be a safe, adequate general controller for a domestic humanoid robot.
entries.note: The 'surely unsafe' part is counterfactual. The 'no viable option at present' part can be checked.

entries.test: Whether any safe, useful domestic humanoid robot or serious general-intelligence candidate existed as of 2022.
entries.note: The 'can't really build' requirement is partly conceptual. Read as a claim about 2022.
